title: Welcome to the Jungle Drops Its Trailer Tomorrow. Bollywood's Most Ridiculous Cast Is Ready.
excerpt: Akshay Kumar, Suniel Shetty, Paresh Rawal, Sanjay Dutt, and roughly half of Bollywood reunite for the Welcome franchise's wildest instalment yet — trailer launches June 11 at a grand event.
body:
The **Welcome** franchise doesn't do subtle. It never has. And from everything we know about **Welcome To The Jungle**, the third instalment isn't about to start now.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=CEfuDgQeROQ</youtube>

Tomorrow, June 11, the makers will drop the theatrical trailer at a grand launch event with the entire cast assembled under one roof — and when we say entire cast, we mean a headcount that rivals a small wedding. **Akshay Kumar**, **Suniel Shetty**, **Paresh Rawal**, **Sanjay Dutt**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Jacqueline Fernandez**, **Disha Patani**, **Raveena Tandon**, **Lara Dutta**, **Jackie Shroff**, **Aftab Shivdasani**, **Johnny Lever**, **Rajpal Yadav**, **Shreyas Talpade**, **Tusshar Kapoor**, **Krushna Abhishek**, **Kiku Sharda**, **Daler Mehndi**, and **Mika Singh**. If you're exhausted just reading that list, imagine the trailer.

The nearly three-minute promo is said to be loaded with the franchise's signature madness — slapstick pileups, situational chaos, and the kind of one-liners that have been running through NRI WhatsApp groups since 2007. Sources tell Pinkvilla that the chemistry between Akshay, Suniel, and Paresh Rawal is the trailer's biggest draw, a reunion of comic timing that's been sorely missed on the big screen.

> "Akshay Kumar will be seen in top form. His camaraderie with Suniel Shetty and Paresh Rawal is sure to remind audiences why the trio has always been loved on screen." — Source close to the production

But here's where it gets interesting. Director **Ahmed Khan** has gone on record calling Welcome 3 "a black dark situational humour" film, not a slapstick comedy. "Firoz Nadiadwala believes in dark humour and situational humour. And of course, it's serious cinema," Khan told Pinkvilla in an earlier interview. Whether that's a tonal reinvention or just the kind of thing directors say to sound elevated, we'll know tomorrow.

The franchise has had a rocky road to get here. Production started over a year ago, was halted, and at one point risked being shelved entirely before the cast reunited for a 15-day final schedule late last year. The fact that it made it to a trailer launch at all is something of a minor miracle.

On the business end, the numbers are already looking healthy. **JioStar** has reportedly locked the domestic theatrical, satellite, and OTT rights — meaning the film will hit JioHotstar after its theatrical run. **Pen Marudhar** is said to be finalizing the overseas theatrical deal, with strong interest from the Middle East, UK, and North American markets. That's the trifecta for any film banking on diaspora love, and the Welcome franchise has always played well in NRI-heavy territories.

**For the diaspora:** the film hits theatres on **June 26**, which means it'll land in US, UK, and Canadian cinemas the same weekend. Given that the franchise's appeal is basically "call your cousins, grab a row, and laugh until you cry," this is a prime candidate for a group outing. The film's release is particularly significant for NRIs, as it offers a chance to reconnect with cultural roots and share laughter with family, bridging the distance that often comes with living abroad. JioHotstar will eventually have it streaming, but the theatrical experience is the real sell here.

The teaser, which dropped unannounced in May, already confirmed the jungle backdrop — think madcap adventure meets ensemble chaos. The songs have been rolling out, including "Ucha Lamba Kad Forever" featuring Akshay and Disha Patani, which leans hard into nostalgia for the original franchise's music. Producer **Firoz Nadiadwala** has assembled what might be the most stacked comedy cast Bollywood has seen in a decade.

Tomorrow's trailer will officially kick off an aggressive promotional campaign leading up to the June 26 release. In a month that already has **Main Vaapas Aaunga**, **Governor**, **Cocktail 2**, and **Balan The Boy** jostling for screens, Welcome to the Jungle needs to come out swinging. Based on the cast, the franchise legacy, and the sheer volume of star power involved — it probably will.

*Welcome To The Jungle is scheduled to release in Indian theatres and key international markets on June 26, 2026. The trailer launches June 11 at a grand event.*
